title: Gomoku Feature State
description: Tracks the lifecycle of a single feature folder under .features/NNN.<slug>/. The file is self-sufficient for an orchestrating AI agent: each stage embeds the full sub-agent definitions (names, personalities, responsibilities), the interaction protocol between them, and machine-readable exit criteria that say when the stage is done and what global state to advance to. The file is created automatically with global state 'initial' and advances through spec → plan → implement → done (and possibly reopened).

$schema.description: Optional pointer back to this schema for editor validation.

number.description: Zero-padded three-digit feature sequence number. Never changes.

slug.description: Short kebab-case feature name agreed on by human and AI before the folder was created.

title.description: Human-readable feature name, e.g. 'Implement Authentication and Authorization'.

directory.description: Repo-relative path of the feature folder containing overview.md, spec.md, plan.md, and this state.json.

state.description: Global lifecycle state of the feature. 'initial' is set when the file is auto-created; it becomes 'spec' the moment the agents start discussing a non-blank spec.md.

history.description: Append-only log of global state transitions.

by.description: Agent or human who triggered the transition.

stages.description: Per-stage tracking hashes. Each stage is self-describing: it defines the sub-agents to spawn (with personalities), the protocol governing their interaction, the running counters/handovers, and the exit criteria that advance the global state.

spec.description: spec.md authoring loop: the Product Manager (Wiggins) drafts, the UX Designer (Cartman) critiques/updates, then the Senior Frontend Engineer (Kyle) signs off with a complexity estimate in points (1 pt ≈ 2 h, 2 pt ≈ 2/3 day, 3 pt ≈ 1 day; additive — 15 pt ≈ one engineer-week).

plan.description: plan.md debate: Wiggins + Jeff Dean (scaling, cost, PostgreSQL 18, UUID PKs, FK/check constraints) + Kiggie (end-to-end proposal, modern React/tooling). Sub-state moves 'planning_in_progress' → 'ready_for_implementation'.

implement.description: Implementation team: Jeff Dean (lead, backend/database), Kiggie (frontend), and Bryce (full-stack DevOps; Terraform + Terragrunt).

status.description: 'agreed' = all participating agents are satisfied and the markdown artifact has been written; 'complete' = the global state has moved past this stage.

sub_state.description: Optional finer-grained label, e.g. 'planning_in_progress' or 'ready_for_implementation' on the plan stage.

current_agent.description: Agent currently holding the pen; null when the stage is not active.

agents.description: Roster of sub-agents for this stage, keyed by agent id. Each entry is a complete definition — name, personality, responsibilities — sufficient for the orchestrating agent to spawn the sub-agent, plus its runtime participation state.

counters.description: How many times the artifact has been criticized, updated, and handed over during this stage.

handovers.description: Chronological hand-over chain between agents within this stage.

artifacts.description: Markdown files this stage produces or mutates, relative to the feature folder.

complexity_points.description: Senior Frontend Engineer's additive point estimate recorded at spec sign-off (1 pt ≈ 2 h, 2 pt ≈ 2/3 day, 3 pt ≈ 1 day).

agent.description: A complete sub-agent definition plus its runtime participation state. The definition fields (name, role, personality, responsibilities, expertise, authority) double as the spawn prompt for the orchestrating agent.

name.description: The agent's name as used in conversation, e.g. 'Wiggins', 'Cartman', 'Kyle', 'Jeff Dean', 'Kiggie', 'Bryce'.

role.description: Job title, e.g. 'Product Manager', 'UX Designer', 'Senior Frontend Engineer'.

personality.description: Character sketch used as the sub-agent's system prompt: background, temperament, heroes, biases, catchphrases.

responsibilities.description: Concrete duties this agent owns during the stage.

expertise.description: Domains the agent is authoritative on, e.g. 'PostgreSQL 18', 'JWT', 'React 19'.

authority.description: 'final_arbiter' resolves all disagreements (Product Manager); 'sign_off' must approve before the stage can exit (e.g. the Frontend Engineer's complexity/security sign-off).

satisfied.description: Runtime: true once the agent has declared 'I am satisfied with this specification/plan'.

criticisms.description: Runtime: criticisms raised by this specific agent.

revisions.description: Runtime: direct edits this agent made to the artifact.

protocol.description: Machine-readable description of how the stage's agents interact and when the stage is finished.

entry_agent.description: Agent that opens the stage (e.g. the Product Manager writes the first draft).

interaction.description: Ordered rules of engagement the orchestrating agent enforces, e.g. 'PM and UX Designer iterate until each says: I am satisfied with this specification, let's bring in the Frontend Engineer.'

satisfaction_phrase.description: The exact phrase an agent must utter to flip its 'satisfied' flag.

max_rounds.description: Optional safety valve: maximum back-and-forth rounds before the final arbiter decides unilaterally.

exit_criteria.description: When ALL of these hold, the stage status becomes 'agreed' and the global state advances.

all_agents_satisfied.description: Every agent in the roster has satisfied=true.

artifacts_written.description: Files that must exist and be non-blank in the feature folder, e.g. ['spec.md'].

required_sign_offs.description: Agents whose explicit sign-off (sign_off_at set) is mandatory, e.g. the Frontend Engineer's complexity estimate.

set_sub_state.description: Sub-state to write on exit, e.g. 'ready_for_implementation' — the point at which the feature is considered ready to implement.

advance_global_state_to.description: Global state the feature moves to once the criteria are met.
